BST 260 Final Project Proposal

Aiden Hai

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

To the BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026

I will study how permitless concealed carry spread across U.S. states from 2014 to 2024 and how firearm mortality changed in adopting states compared with states that continued to require permits.

Vignette 1. How did state concealed-carry permit rules change from 2014 to 2024?

I will use the dates when rules took effect and were replaced to determine which rule was in place in each state each year. I will identify which states removed the permit requirement and which states kept it but changed how they issued permits. Then I will compare when and where these changes happened. I will use gunleg, which contains policy records and references to state laws from the RAND State Firearm Law Database. The finalproject package includes a copy of the data.

data("gunleg", package = "finalproject")

I will use the following methods to build and compare state policy histories.

  • Record filtering (filter()). Keep the laws about concealed carry. Include older laws so I can tell what rules each state had at the start of 2014.
  • Date sorting (arrange()). Put each state’s laws in order by when they took effect. This will show when the state first dropped the permit requirement and when it made later changes. If a date is unclear, I will check the law itself.
  • Cross-tabulation. Count how many states in each region switched from each type of permit rule. Mark cases where I cannot confirm the earlier rule.
  • Annual adoption counts. Count each state once, in the year it first dropped the permit requirement. Use these counts to see which years had the most changes.
  • State timeline plot. Give each state one row and color each year by the permit rule in place. Mark the year a state dropped the permit requirement if it did.
  • Cumulative adoption curves. For each year, show what percentage of states in each region had dropped the requirement by then. Percentages make it easier to compare regions with different numbers of states.

Vignette 2. How did firearm mortality change after adoption?

For each group of states that dropped the permit requirement in the same year, I will look at how firearm death rates changed before and after the law took effect. I will compare that change with what happened over the same years in states that still required permits throughout that period. I will check whether the two groups’ rates were already changing differently before the law took effect and discuss whether other policy changes might help explain the results. I will use cdcfiremort, which contains annual age-adjusted firearm death rates per 100,000 residents from CDC/NCHS. The finalproject package includes a copy of these data.

data("cdcfiremort", package = "finalproject")

I will use the following methods to compare mortality and assess uncertainty.

  • Table join (left_join()). Add each state’s adoption year to its mortality records. Check that there is one row for each state and year.
  • Three-year comparison windows. Compare three full years before the law took effect with three full years after. Skip the year it took effect and use the same calendar years for both groups.
  • Group-mean line plots. Plot the average death rate for each group in each year. Look at the years before the law took effect to see whether the groups were already moving in different directions.
  • Group-by-period interaction (lm()). For each adoption year, estimate how much more or less the death rate changed in states that dropped the requirement than in states that kept it. Report the difference in deaths per 100,000 people.
  • 95% confidence intervals. Calculate one before-and-after change for each state. Use those changes to estimate how uncertain the difference between the two groups is.
  • Two-year window check. Repeat the comparison with the same states, using two years before and two years after. Check whether the estimated difference changes in size or direction.
  • Comparison group check. Repeat the analysis using only comparison states whose permit rules stayed the same during the years being compared. Check whether the estimated difference changes.

AI Use Disclosure

  • AI tool: ChatGPT
  • How I Used AI
    • I first used ChatGPT to organize the datasets that appeared in the course lecture and assignments (as well as those listed in finalproject instruction), to brainstorm as many topics where two datasets could be combined. I then compared them based on criterias like correlation strength, analysis difficulty. I selected the “gunleg” and “cdcfiremort” datasets, and then asked it to help assess whether these data were sufficient and whether additional data was needed. After determining the topic and the exact research questions for the two vignettes myself, I asked the AI to remind of me which methods to apply. After listing the methods I planned to use, I asked it to check whether each method could address the research questions for each vignette.
Prompts Used (Summary)
  • Which datasets covered in the course can be combined for analysis? How do the various combinations compare in terms of relevance, analytical complexity, and novelty?
  • I selected “gunleg” and “cdcfiremort.” Is the existing data sufficient to compare changes in mortality rates before and after the policy took effect? Do I need to supplement it with additional data?
  • For these two vignettes, what methods can be applied? Can each method I listed address the corresponding research question?
